definitions.explanation: A word of Chinese origin in the Japanese language, typically written in kanji and read with on'yomi (Chinese-derived readings). One of the three main vocabulary strata in Japanese, alongside wago (native Japanese) and gairaigo (Western loanwords).

examples.japanese: 「⟦{図書館|としょかん}→図書館：00580_toshokan⟧」⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{漢語|かんご}だ。
⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{語彙|ごい}→語彙：14214_goi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{多|おお}く⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{漢語|かんご}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{占|し}めている→占める：11799_shimeru⟧。
examples.english: A large portion of Japanese vocabulary consists of Sino-Japanese words.

examples.japanese: ⟦{論文|ろんぶん}→論文：03787_ronbun⟧や⟦{公文書|こうぶんしょ}→公文書：11677_koubunsho⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{和語|わご}→和語：12074_wago⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{漢語|かんご}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}く→多い：01127_ooi⟧⟦{使|つか}われる→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦{傾向|けいこう}→傾向：02695_keikou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: In academic papers and official documents, Sino-Japanese words tend to be used more than native Japanese words.

notes:
USAGE:
A linguistics term used in discussions of Japanese vocabulary composition. Japanese vocabulary is traditionally divided into three strata: ⟦{和語|わご}→和語：12074_wago⟧ (native Japanese words), {漢語|かんご} (Sino-Japanese words), and ⟦{外来語|がいらいご}→外来語：12101_gairaigo⟧ (loanwords from Western languages). {漢語|かんご} makes up roughly 50% of dictionary headwords in Japanese.

{漢語|かんご} words are typically read with ⟦{音読|おんよ}み→音読み：10453_onyomi⟧ (on'yomi, Chinese-derived readings) and tend to sound more formal or academic than their ⟦{和語|わご}→和語：12074_wago⟧ equivalents.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {漢語|かんご}⟦{由来|ゆらい}→由来：05451_yurai⟧: of Sino-Japanese origin
- ⟦{和語|わご}→和語：12074_wago⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{漢語|かんご}: native words and Sino-Japanese words
- {漢語|かんご}⟦{表現|ひょうげん}→表現：03584_hyougen⟧: Sino-Japanese expression
